finding: The root's own header states that the brand syncs from the workspace shared theme; no sync exists in either direction, so the panel's framing sentence is false.
evidence: 1747:8392 reads 'Everyday styling lives here. The brand syncs from your workspace shared theme.' DesignSystemTab.tsx:657 renders that sentence verbatim and DesignSystemTab.tsx:663 is the only behaviour behind the strip — window.open(`${DASHBOARD_URL}/dashboard/agency/theme`) in a new tab. Per W-CO-01 the server's theme router (12 procedures incl. applyPreset/list/save/delete) has zero editor callers; independently verified here — grep for theme.applyPreset|theme.list|theme.save|theme.delete|themeSync across packages/editor/src returns nothing, and packages/editor/src/services/ holds cmsSync.ts, componentSync.ts and templateSync.ts with no themeSync.ts.
fix: Either wire the theme router (a themeSync.ts beside its three siblings), or change 1747:8392 to say what is true — the shared theme is a starting point opened in the dashboard, and edits here stay on this site.

finding: CONFIRMED DEAD (the census's only candidate) — and worse in code than on the board: both recovery buttons on a failed schema migration only close the dialog.
evidence: 433:2439 'btn/primary' (Restore snapshot) has no reaction on itself or any ancestor; 433:2391 is the one board in the section with no frame-level reaction, which is why it is the only census hit. In code MigrationProgressMount.tsx:122-129 handleRestoreSnapshot does nothing but setOpen(false) — its own comment reads 'Phase F.2 will wire a real restore action … For now we just close.' MigrationProgressMount.tsx:131-136 handleRetry is identical ('For now we close'). So 433:2441 'btn/secondary' (Retry v3), which does carry a Figma reaction → 153:120, is equally dead in the product. boards.json records 433:2391 as authority open:migration-ui-unbuilt — an open question, not a declared block.
fix: Until the restore path exists, replace both buttons with the honest state the mount actually produces (a close and the existing fail-soft toast). A button labelled 'Restore snapshot' that discards the dialog and leaves the project stuck is the worst available option.

finding: Every component row draws a chevron and has no destination on the board AND no onClick in the shipping panel — 27 rows that look like drill-ins and are inert.
evidence: Board rows 153:36 Hero · 153:39 Menu card · 153:42 Booking form · 153:45 Footer · 153:48 Gallery · 153:51 Testimonial, each carrying its own '›' text node (153:38/41/44/47/50/53), none with a reaction. finding: The last confirmation before a brand-wide apply can only describe 3 of the 14 token registries and cannot show a removal, so editing a radius, shadow or motion token produces a blank "Review 0 staged changes" over an enabled "Apply 0 changes".
evidence: DesignSystemTab.tsx:350 tokensDirty = allRegistries.reduce(...) — all 14 registries feed the footer and the root's dirty dot. ReviewModal is handed only colour, type and spacing (DesignSystemTab.tsx:858-863) and computes totalChanges from exactly those three (ReviewModal.tsx:84-93). ReviewModal.tsx:206-207 renders `Apply {totalChanges} changes` with no disabled guard, and onConfirm → handleApply persists every registry. The board draws two rows the modal has no code path for: 'radius/card 8 → 12' and 'shadow/raised removed' — ReviewModal has three sections (Color / Typography / Spacing, :121 and :175-176) and one row shape, name/was/now (:47-63).
fix: Pass all 14 registries into ReviewModal and add a removal row shape; at minimum disable Apply when totalChanges is 0 so the modal cannot claim a change set it did not read.

finding: The add-token form is drawn nowhere — the board is the kinds list with a badge dropped on top of it, while the code requires two fields and raises three validation errors none of which appear on any board.
evidence: 306:2049 is a copy of 152:52 (rows 306:2053 color … 306:2073 motion) plus 333:2348 'Badge' at y=84, which lands on top of 306:2053 'Kind · color' (y=80). AddTokenModal.tsx:16-43 is a real dialog: 'Token name' TextInput (:88-105), 'Hex value' with swatch (:110-130), and validate() (:22-39) produces 'Name is required' (:26), 'A token with this name already exists' (:29) and 'Enter a valid 6-digit hex color' (:34). None of the four — the two fields and the two error states — is drawn. The modal also only creates colour tokens (onAdd → handleAddToken, DesignSystemTab.tsx:597+ builds category:"colors"), while 152:52 offers six kinds.
fix: Draw the modal — title, both fields with the swatch, both error states — and say on it that it adds a colour token only, or widen the code to the kind the user drilled into.

finding: The import screen's central promise — apply the valid rows and skip the broken ones — is refused by the parser, which is all-or-nothing, so the numbers the board draws cannot occur together.
evidence: The board's summary reads 'Detected 24 · Valid 22 · Errors 2 · Conflicts 1' over a primary button 'Apply 22 valid only'. importUtils.ts:108 — `if (errors.length > 0) return { tokens: [], errors };` — one malformed token rejects the whole file. ImportCard.tsx:170-178 then sets parseErrors, fires onOutcome('import-failed') and setParsed(null) and returns, so the detail block and the error list are mutually exclusive; ImportCard.tsx:186 sets errors:[] unconditionally on the success branch, which means the board's 'Errors' row (rendered at ImportCard.tsx:348-355) can only ever print '0'.
fix: Founder precedence puts behaviour on the code side, so either make parseImportJSON partial (return the good tokens alongside the errors) or redraw the board's summary and button for the all-or-nothing contract that ships.

finding: "See which components use a token before changing it" is one of the four jobs this module exists for, and the screen that answers it has no board — only the collapsed count.

TokenDetailView.tsx:462-495 renders the expanded list: one row per binding, labelled with the element type and the styleProp it binds (:487-489), each clickable to select that element on canvas (:474-479 composer.selection.select(target)). usageExpanded state at :155.

finding: Applying a starter is one unconfirmed click that also wipes the token undo stack, and the only route back discards every unrelated staged edit with it.
evidence: Confirm: none. StartersSection.tsx:39-45 choose() calls applyStarter immediately on card click; the board's warning (152:137, 'Applying a starter overwrites your tokens.', StartersSection.tsx:65) is the whole of the guard. Undo: useApplyStarter.ts:63-65 stages via stageTokens, and useTokenBase.ts:139-149 stageTokens does setTokens(next) plus setUndoStack({}) and setRedoStack({}) — per-token undo is destroyed by the apply. Way back: only discardAll (useTokenBase.ts:122-127, reverting to savedTokens), invoked by handleDiscard across all 14 token registries and all preset registries at once (DesignSystemTab.tsx:573-574). Per W-CO-01 there is no server copy to fall back on either. The apply-time toast has no Undo action; the only Undo action in the panel hangs off Discard (DesignSystemTab.tsx:578-583).
fix: Confirm on the card click, naming the starter and how many tokens it replaces; or keep a single-step 'Undo <starter>' on the applied state, which is the one recovery that does not take the user's other edits with it.

finding: The board that confirms a starter was applied is orphaned — nothing in the section points at it, so in the prototype the destructive action gives no acknowledgement.

finding: FINE, not dead — the "Fix ›" link is a declared design-ahead state, but its chevron implies a destination that will never exist and the board's closing note contradicts the shipped copy.

finding: The import flow's one decision — what to do about ID collisions — is drawn on no board, although the board's own sample data puts the user in exactly the state that raises it.

finding: Two boards in this family advertise a file type the importer rejects — a dropped .css returns a JSON parse error.

finding: The preset board's category list does not match the product's: two of its six rows name categories that do not exist, and seven real categories have no row.

finding: The AI generation job cannot be finished — the success state offers only Discard and Retry, because the schema it produces has nowhere to go.

finding: The only AI entry point in the module has no edge to the modal it opens; the modal is reachable in the prototype only from a parked state chip on a board that draws no AI control.
